title: Introduction to Strategic Management
outcomes: Explain strategy, strategic decisions and strategic management.
Discuss the importance and limitations of strategic management.
Formulate vision, mission, goals, objectives and values.
Distinguish corporate, business and functional strategy.

meta.exam_tip: In case questions, quote the fact from the case and tie it to the concept — examiners reward application.

concepts.title: Strategy and strategic management
body: Strategy is a long-range, integrated plan that sets the direction and scope of an organisation and positions it to gain advantage in a changing environment. It is partly planned (deliberate) and partly emerging from responses to events.
Strategic management is the continuous process of analysing the environment, setting direction, choosing strategies, implementing them and evaluating results to achieve long-term objectives.
Strategic decisions are future-oriented, involve large commitments of resources, affect the whole organisation, are taken by top management, and are often hard to reverse.
concepts.analogy: Strategy is the game plan; strategic management is coaching the team through the whole season.
concepts.work: A mobile phone maker deciding to manufacture in India rather than import is a strategic decision.

concepts.title: Importance and limitations of strategic management
body: Importance: gives a clear direction; helps anticipate change; allocates resources to priorities; builds sustainable competitive advantage; improves coordination; and prepares the firm to handle risks and opportunities.

Limitations: environment is complex and fast-changing, so plans can become outdated; strategic planning is time-consuming and costly; long-term predictions are uncertain; and success depends on implementation, which plans alone cannot guarantee.
Strategic management works best when combined with flexibility and learning.
concepts.analogy: A strategy is useful only if the organisation can adapt it as the world changes.
concepts.work: Many retailers had to rewrite plans quickly when online shopping surged.

concepts.title: Strategic intent: vision, mission, goals, objectives and values
body: Strategic intent is the leveraging of resources and capabilities to achieve a desired future; it is expressed through vision, mission, goals and objectives, and values.

Vision describes what the organisation aspires to become; mission defines its purpose, customers, products and philosophy; goals are broad results; objectives are specific, measurable and time-bound targets that operationalise goals.
Values are the shared beliefs that guide behaviour. A good mission is clear, feasible, motivating and distinctive; objectives should be SMART and consistent with each other.
concepts.analogy: Vision points to the destination; mission explains the journey; objectives mark the milestones.
concepts.work: "Clean energy for every home" is a vision; "install 10 lakh solar roofs by 2030" is an objective.

concepts.title: Levels of strategy
body: Corporate-level strategy decides which businesses to be in and how to allocate resources among them (growth, stability, retrenchment, diversification).
Business-level strategy decides how each business unit competes in its market (cost leadership, differentiation, focus).

Functional-level strategy covers marketing, finance, operations, HR and R&D plans supporting business strategy. The three levels form a network: corporate sets the frame, business adapts it to markets, functions execute — with feedback flowing upward.
concepts.analogy: Corporate asks "where?", business asks "how?", functions ask "with what actions?".
concepts.work: A group choosing to exit cement is corporate; its cement unit's pricing plan is business; the plant's maintenance plan is functional.

illustrations.title: Writing strategic intent
illustrations.q: GreenRide is an Indian start-up that rents electric scooters in cities. Draft a vision, a mission, two goals, two measurable objectives and two values for it, and explain how each differs.

head: Element
Example for GreenRide
What it does
rows: Cities where every short trip is clean, cheap and quick
Describes the desired long-term future; inspiring, not measurable
We provide affordable, app-based electric scooter rentals that make urban commuting greener
States purpose, customers and business scope today
Become the most trusted e-mobility brand in tier-2 cities; build a profitable charging network
Reach 50,000 monthly riders by March 2028; cut cost per ride by 15% in two years
Safety first; honesty with riders and partners

jobs.title: Board strategy workshop
jobs.situation: A family business asks for help writing its first vision and mission.
jobs.takeaway: Strategic intent turns family ambitions into shared, measurable direction.

mcqs.explain: They commit significant resources and shape the future. In practice: made by top management.

mcqs.q: Which statement describes "what we want to become"?
mcqs.explain: Vision expresses the desired future state. In practice: mission explains present purpose.
mcqs.topic: Strategic intent: vision, mission, goals, objectives and values

mcqs.q: Objectives differ from goals because they are:
mcqs.explain: Objectives make goals operational. In practice: use SMART criteria.
mcqs.topic: Strategic intent: vision, mission, goals, objectives and values

mcqs.q: Deciding which industries a group should operate in is:
mcqs.explain: Portfolio scope is a corporate decision. In practice: involves acquisitions and exits.

mcqs.q: A limitation of strategic management is:
options: Plans may become outdated in a fast-changing environment
mcqs.explain: Uncertainty and change can make plans obsolete. In practice: review strategies periodically.
mcqs.topic: Importance and limitations of strategic management

mcqs.q: How a business unit competes against rivals is decided at the:
mcqs.explain: Business strategy addresses competitive positioning. In practice: cost leadership or differentiation choices.

options: Leveraging resources and capabilities to reach a desired future
mcqs.explain: It is expressed through vision, mission, goals, objectives and values. In practice: aligns the organisation.
mcqs.topic: Strategic intent: vision, mission, goals, objectives and values

mcqs.q: An emergent strategy is one that:
options: Develops from responses to unforeseen events
mcqs.explain: Realised strategy often blends deliberate plans and emergent responses. In practice: stay adaptable.

summary: Strategy: long-term direction and scope; deliberate plus emergent.
Strategic decisions: long-term, resource-heavy, top-level, hard to reverse.
Vision → mission → goals → SMART objectives; values guide conduct.

viva.model: A continuous process of analysing the environment, setting direction, choosing and implementing strategies and evaluating results to achieve long-term objectives.
Vision describes the desired future the organisation aspires to; mission states its current purpose, customers and scope.

viva.q: Give two limitations of strategic management.
viva.model: The environment changes quickly so plans may become outdated, and the process is time-consuming and costly.

viva.q: Name the three levels of strategy.
viva.model: Corporate level, business level and functional level.
It should be specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound, and consistent with the mission.

cases.title: Saffron Foods Group
cases.case: Saffron Foods Group runs packaged snacks, a restaurant chain and a dairy. The board plans to sell the dairy, the snacks business wants to compete on low prices, and the restaurant chain's HR team designs a new training programme. The group's statement reads: "To bring healthy Indian flavours to every family."

mcqs.explain: Exiting a business changes the group's portfolio. In practice: decided by the board.

mcqs.q: Competing on low prices in snacks is a:
mcqs.explain: It concerns how one business competes. In practice: requires cost efficiency.

mcqs.q: The HR training programme is a:
mcqs.explain: It supports the restaurant business through one function. In practice: linked to service quality.

mcqs.q: "To bring healthy Indian flavours to every family" is best described as a:
mcqs.explain: It is broad and inspirational, not measurable. In practice: needs objectives to measure progress.
mcqs.topic: Strategic intent: vision, mission, goals, objectives and values
